strength: strong mathematical structure; physical method transfer untested
sharedBottleneck: A relative observation can determine a product or ratio while leaving the absolute scale and calibration factor inseparable.

variableMapping.digitalTwin: traceable reference artefact or independent calibration channel

variableMapping.role: tests the inferred calibration rather than reusing the relative sensor

conditionsForTransfer: The nuisance enters approximately as a constant multiplicative scale over the tested domain.
The relative data and absolute calibration are generated by independent measurement chains.
Model-shape parameters are either identified or profiled rather than silently absorbed into the scale.
failureBoundary: The mapping fails when calibration drift is state-dependent, hysteretic, or nonmultiplicative.
BAO-only scale symmetry is broken by adding full early-universe physics, independent clocks, or other absolute-distance information; the resulting inference is no longer the same problem.
A common upstream reference makes two nominally independent calibrations correlated and can create false agreement.
minimumValidation: Create two scale-equivalent synthetic worlds. The estimator must refuse to report h and r_d, or x and g, separately from relative data alone. Add one traceably independent absolute observation and require recovery of both factors with calibrated coverage. Repeat after introducing drift to locate where the mapping breaks.

rc61Evidence.interpretation: The same BAO likelihood supports different H0/r_d pairs until an external absolute calibration is supplied.

validationStatus: The cosmological product symmetry is analytic and reproduced numerically. Transfer to a physical digital twin has not been tested on sensor data.
